title: MIMO multi-input/output heads versus shared Mirror member views
hypothesis: For member tasks with rotation-aligned linear heads, a shared head plus per-member Mirror phase preserves MIMO member quality/diversity with fewer bytes and one batched evaluation; generic low-rank coefficient coding may match it.
physical_object: one shared 8D logistic head or MIMO member-head bank
mirror_coordinate: one learned planar angle per member acting on first two head coordinates
logical_multiplicity: eight member-specific binary classifiers evaluated in one batched call

task.teacher: rotate first two coordinates of one shared logistic weight vector by evenly spaced member phases

controls: MIMO-style independent member heads trained/evaluated as one stacked batch
shared Mirror head plus per-member learned phases
shared generic rank-2 basis plus two coefficients/member

development.selection_metric: member NLL/ECE/accuracy, pairwise disagreement/correlation, actual bytes and batch throughput

storage.authority: actual deterministic serialized inference payload bytes
paid_objects: shared head or all member heads

success_gate: Mirror mean NLL within .02 and disagreement within .02 of MIMO; payload <=.80x MIMO and <=.90x generic coefficient control; one-batch inference retained.
failure_gate: Mirror misses NLL/diversity or generic coefficient control is within 10% bytes and quality.
boundaries: linear MIMO analogue, not deep PA42 reproduction
fixed update evidence is not capacity
no natural diversity or uncertainty claim
